evidence_quotes.quote: The water allocation institutions or system is the set of rules that are used to determine and to share the available water resources among different users.
The water allocation process concerns the water impounded by dams. Therefore, the case studies selected for this analysis were located in the north of Tunisia (Figure 1).
Document review, meetings observation, data examination and interviews allow gathering of factual information on the water allocation system and related decision-making process.

The Ichkeul use refers only to the volume of water supplied specifically to the Ichkeul lake, whereas the environmental use is the sum of the volume for groundwater recharge and the Ichkeul use in addition to releases related to dam operations, which still may have some ecological benefits for Ichkeul lake. The urban use is the volume of water allocated to the SONEDE.
The data display information on areas by crops and water billed in Buherthma irrigated land. The required data on Buherthma dam’s releases were provided by the Ministry of Agriculture as well.

criterion_notes.c1: No. The paper is a basin-scale surface water resources and agricultural irrigation allocation study (Exclusion Criterion 7: water-resource studies unrelated to household or community service access). Its two empirical case studies examine reservoir releases across macro-sectors (bulk raw-water allocation to SONEDE, agriculture, and Ichkeul Lake ecological flows) and irrigation quotas across strategic vs. non-strategic crops in Buherthma irrigated farmlands. A single sentence citing national WHO/UNICEF JMP drinking-water coverage in Section 4.1 is background context rather than an analysis of household or community service access.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording: YES — the study examines a legal, administrative, and institutional governance factor, specifically Tunisia's centralized administrative priority-queuing water-allocation institution under the 1975 Water Act, seasonal irrigation allocation plans by the Ministry of Agriculture, and restrictions on trading water rights. Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: NO — the rule-type mechanism analysed governs bulk reservoir raw-water releases across macro-sectors (urban utility bulk supply, agriculture, ecological flows) and crop-specific agricultural irrigation rationing rather than rules directly governing household or community water or sanitation service access (such as connection eligibility, tenure/documentation rules, household tariffs, or disconnection). Note that even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the overall study decision remains exclude because Criteria 1 and 4 fail.
criterion_notes.c3: Yes. Mixed-methods empirical study combining document review, closed-meeting observations at the Ministry of Agriculture, stakeholder interviews, and nonparametric first-order stochastic dominance (empirical CDF) analysis of administrative dam-release and irrigation-billing records from Ichkeul watershed (1990-2012) and Buherthma basin (1999-2011).
criterion_notes.c4: No. Reported empirical outcomes are annual/seasonal bulk reservoir release volumes (million m3) and sectoral/crop supply-reliability distributions (eCDFs for bulk urban transfers to SONEDE, agricultural water releases, Ichkeul Lake environmental releases, and strategic vs. non-strategic irrigated crop allocations), not household or community WASH access, connection, continuity, quantity, or affordability outcomes.
criterion_notes.c5: Yes. For its water-resources research question, the paper clearly identifies the units of analysis (two northern Tunisian watersheds/hydrosystems—Ichkeul 1990-2012 and Buherthma irrigated perimeter 1999-2011—partitioned by sectoral and crop demand categories), exposure (priority-queuing administrative reservoir allocation rule), outcomes (reservoir release volumes and stochastic dominance/supply reliability), and study design (comparative mixed-methods case study).
criterion_notes.c6: Yes. Full text is written in English.

study_design: Mixed-methods comparative case study combining document review, institutional meeting observations, stakeholder interviews, and quantitative nonparametric first-order stochastic dominance (eCDF) analysis of administrative reservoir-release time series
population_and_sample: Two northern Tunisian river sub-basins / reservoir hydrosystems: Ichkeul watershed (Sejnane, Joumine, and Ghazala dam releases, 1990-2012) and Buherthma basin irrigated perimeter (24,000 ha irrigated farmlands and Buherthma dam releases, 1999-2011), plus Ministry of Agriculture allocation meetings and stakeholder interviews
exposure: Centralized priority-queuing administrative surface-water allocation rules implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture for reservoir releases across sectors (urban bulk SONEDE demand, agriculture, ecological flows) and crop classes (strategic vs. non-strategic crops)
outcome: Bulk reservoir water release volumes (10^6 m^3) and empirical cumulative distribution functions / first-order stochastic dominance (supply reliability) across urban bulk, agricultural, and environmental uses and strategic vs. non-strategic irrigated crops
rationale: Excluded under E01 (Wrong topic — Exclusion Criterion 7: water-resource studies unrelated to household or community service access). The paper empirically investigates basin-scale surface-water reservoir releases and priority-queuing rules across macro-sectors (bulk raw-water allocation to the national utility SONEDE, irrigated agriculture, and Ichkeul Lake environmental flows) and between strategic and non-strategic irrigated crops. It does not empirically examine household or community water or sanitation service access, connections, affordability, or household-level access outcomes (failing c1 and c4, as well as the narrow service-access rule-type scope of c2).
